courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Currently, our application uses the default Ionic theme which uses a blue primary color.
Now I want to use different colors
and how do we do that? In our code,
you will find that theme folder and there you find the variables.scss file. In here,
these here, these things with the two dashes at the beginning are CSS variables.
They have to start with two dashes at the beginning to separate them from normal CSS rules
and these things here can be configured to your likings.
Here we're storing a bunch of colors in hex format and RGB values but you can also set up CSS variables
that store paddings, so something like pixel values or rems, so you can not just store colors but
of course colors are a very prominent use case.
Now here you see the nine colors Ionic gives you to choose from and you can now fine tune every single
one.
So for example if we go to the primary color which is the color we mostly use in this app thus far,
then here in VSCode I can hover over that
to get this color picker and then here, I want to choose a different color,
so let's say I want to use something like this color, a reddish color.
If I choose that and I only change that first variable here and I now save that, the app will reload
and it automatically uses this color you see here on the button already
and you also see it here in the tab bar, in the segmented control, on the hamburger icon here, on this
button.
And that is the amazing thing,
you get this change out of the box with only one change in your code
and that's the idea behind theming and these global rules.
You set up your global variables here and Ionic consumes them automatically because it's still such
that it uses these variables and therefore, you can change your settings in no time and apply your own
theme when it comes to coloring here
but you're not restricted to coloring.
You can also set other things as well
and for that, let's dive into these advanced theming guide here temporarily and let's have a look and
scroll down to globals there in the application variables
and there you see you could also set ion-font-family to set your general font family in the application
or ion-margin to set the general margin that will be used, for example when you're using the margin
utility attribute but also the margin some components use as a default anyways.
So for example here, let's say we add ion, so --ion-padding, set this to 10rem which is
an extremely large value
and then I have a look at the auth page, there
I'm using the padding attribute on ion-content, so therefore now as this reloads,
you see we have the large padding here.
Now obviously that is way too large but it shows you how easy it is for you to adjust this to your requirements
and change the overall padding on your application.
Probably not to 10rem if you want to have a nice application but still if you're fine tuning this to
not use the default of 16 pixels but you want 14 pixels, you can set it like this.
Now I'm happy with the default and hence I'll comment this out but nonetheless, you can set it up just
like that.
